description: The sanctioned-drift registry for the Stage 128 backwards-compatibility suite (tools/hls-compat.py). Every entry names ONE exact historical program (file basename + content sha256-16) whose behaviour drifted between its own release and today's toolchain, together with the sanctioned change responsible and the release that migrated the in-tree fixture. Three kinds: 'break' — the program ran green at its release and today's toolchain fails it (a regression the ledger names); 'resurrect' — the program was red at its own release (a toolchain bug) and runs green today (a drift that must be owned); 'drift' — the program still exits 0 on both toolchains but its output changed (the entry pins both stdout digests and the last old-behaviour release, so any further drift of the same program fails the witness). Anything the current toolchain rejects that is NOT listed here is a regression, not a break; any unnamed resurrection or divergence is a problem, not a pass. The diff is two-way: an entry whose program runs green again (for a break) or fails again (for a resurrect) is drift the tool reports and fails on until the ledger is trimmed. Draft new entries with `python3 tools/hls-compat.py --update-ledger`, review them, and splice them in by hand — the tool never writes this file. The ledger was built from a full-history time-travel sweep (`--time-travel all`) over every release tag: 170 tags, 24,591 corpus instances, every divergence accounted for below.

waivers.reason: The fixture imported "../modules/helper.hls" — a '..' segment. The deep-scan-19 hardening rejects absolute import paths and any '..' segment (a local-file-inclusion vector for services that compile untrusted HLS: import "../../../etc/passwd" used to load host files as source). The historical program is rejected by design; the security property outranks the corpus entry. The guard landed at v0.51.1-alpha but the migrated fixture only shipped at v0.60.0-alpha — for those nine releases the corpus carried an entry its own interpreter rejected (a migration gap the time-travel witness surfaced: old exit 1, today exit 1).
waivers.migrated_in: v0.60.0-alpha (deep-scan-21): the in-tree fixture moved its helper to tests/ok/modules/ and imports downward

waivers.reason: The fixture pinned int operands to 32-bit register names (in("edx") / out("eax")). Stage 83 made named registers bind the FULL 64-bit register, so a 32-bit name on an int operand is a compile error with the fix spelled out (use 'rdx'/'rax'). Silently truncating an int operand to its low 32 bits was a miscompilation, not compatibility.
waivers.migrated_in: v0.102.0-alpha: the in-tree fixture uses rdx/rax with the %b0/%w1 modifiers preserved

waivers.reason: Same rule as its sibling fixture: out("eax") on an int operand. The perfection corpus ran the narrow-register form through every codegen path, so it is the louder of the two witnesses that Stage 83 closed a real hole rather than a theoretical one.
waivers.migrated_in: v0.102.0-alpha: the in-tree fixture uses rax

waivers.reason: The fixture asserted hex64(0) == "0x0" — the old minimal-digit formatting. Stage 85 renders a full 64-bit WORD (16 digits, unsigned) because boot protocols are full of unsigned 64-bit values that arrive in an int as negative numbers. The historical program still compiles and still runs on both of today's backends — it exits 108, its own self-check for the changed expectation. A behavioural change in a formatting primitive, not a language break.
waivers.migrated_in: v0.104.0-alpha: the in-tree fixture asserts the 16-digit form

waivers.reason: The old std.hash xxHash64 was wrong for EVERY input class — the merge round used the wrong multiplier/rotation/primes, the 8-byte tail path was missing entirely, the 1-byte tail ADDed where the spec XORs, the 4-byte tail used a wrong formula. The spec-correct digests fail the historical fixture's pinned expectations, so the program runs to its own check and panics (exit 101) — a behavioural break invisible to the exit-code census, caught by the time-travel witness. The wrong digests were a bug shipped for 21 releases; the spec is the contract.
waivers.migrated_in: v0.83.0-alpha: test vectors updated to the libxxhash reference values

waivers.sanctioned_change: config: a quoted key containing a dot was write-only
waivers.reason: The fixture's toml_quoted read-back check (another.key: expected 2) panicked under every release that shipped this content from the bug's landing — v0.100.1-alpha (the TOML parser rewrite) through v0.109.0-alpha, ten releases — because std.config wrote quoted dotted keys into the table but could not read them back. The suite's own 101-is-green convention masked the red. Before the bug landed (v0.79.0-alpha through v0.100.0-alpha) the same content ran green under its own interpreter AND runs green today — plain agreement. The historical program is red at its own release and green today in the bug window: an unnamed resurrection would be an unowned behavioural change; this entry owns it.
waivers.migrated_in: v0.110.0-alpha: the quoted-dot-key fix and the fixture's read-back check landed together

waivers.sanctioned_change: the project renamed from Hieu Louis to Halis (v0.20.0-alpha)
waivers.reason: The fixture reads the first line of examples/data.txt and echoes it. The data file said "Hieu Louis is a programming language" until v0.19.0-alpha and says "Halis is a programming language" from v0.20.0-alpha — the project-wide rename. The program still compiles, still runs, still exits 0 on both toolchains; its output simply carries the new name. The fixture is not hermetic (it reads live repo data), which is exactly what this entry records.
waivers.migrated_in: v0.20.0-alpha: examples/data.txt carries the Halis name

waivers.sanctioned_change: the project renamed from Hieu Louis to Halis (v0.20.0-alpha)
waivers.reason: The fixture sanitizes and echoes lines from examples/data.txt; the rename changed every line it prints ("Hieu Louis is high-security and high-performance" and friends). Both toolchains exit 0; only the echoed name changed. From v0.8.0-alpha (where this content was born, after html_escape learned to escape the forward slash) through v0.19.0-alpha the old and new outputs differ on exactly those lines.
waivers.migrated_in: v0.20.0-alpha: examples/data.txt carries the Halis name

waivers.reason: The fixture prints html_escape of a script tag without asserting its exact form. Until v0.7.0-alpha the closing slash passed through untouched ("</script>"); from v0.8.0-alpha it is escaped as "/" — closing the classic "</script>" XSS vector. Both toolchains exit 0; the historical program's output differs from today's on that one line. A security hardening, the same family as the deep-scan-19 import guard.
waivers.migrated_in: v0.8.0-alpha: the fixture output shows the escaped slash
